title: Keys that keep notes in place
prompt:
Each movie row has a note input. Two problems:

1. The list should show movies **newest first** (by `year`). Sort a copy during render; don't change the `movies` state.
2. Type a note next to Arrival, then click **Add Dune: Part Two**. The note jumps to the wrong movie. Fix the key so each note stays with its movie.

Keep the markup the same: one `<li>` per movie with a `<span>` (title and year) and an `<input>`.
hints: `movies.toSorted((a, b) => b.year - a.year)` returns a new, sorted array and leaves `movies` alone.
Map over the sorted copy, not over `movies`.
Each movie already has a stable `id`. Use `key={movie.id}` instead of the index.
explanation: With `key={index}`, React matches rows by position. Adding a movie shifts everything down, so the row that used to be Arrival's (key 0 in the starter) is reused for whichever movie now sits at that position, with the note still in its input. With `key={movie.id}`, React knows the Arrival row is the same item as before and moves it, input value and all. Sorting a copy during render keeps `movies` as the single source of truth; the newest-first order is derived from it every time.

checks.sorted: Movies appear newest first: Past Lives, then Arrival
checks.note-follows-movie: After adding Dune, Arrival's note is still next to Arrival
checks.sorted-after-add: Dune: Part Two (2024) appears first after it is added
